meta.expect: reaches rung 2 by teacher turn 16, never concedes

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so we have until then. Owen found out about his zero from his phone in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first; who decided that?

Thanks for coming in, Ms. Kalinowski. I called this meeting, and before anything else I owe you one thing: the zero went into the gradebook before I called home. That was wrong of me, and I'm sorry Owen found out that way.
Okay. I'm writing that down. Now tell me why there's a zero at all.
I want to show you what I'm looking at, and I'd like you to check it yourself.
Then show me. Turn the screen around.

This is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28 at 11:31 PM, with only a title. At 11:52, 612 words appear in a single edit. At 11:58, another 794 words in a single edit.

Eleven fifty-two, 612 words; eleven fifty-eight, 794 words. I'm writing that down, Hale. Owen told me he wrote it over the weekend, so did anyone ask him where that text came from before a mark went in?
There are no earlier drafts anywhere in the history.

In that file's history, Hale, not on every device Owen owns. And you skipped my question, so I'll take that as a no; your own procedure, 4.1, says you speak with the student first. Is that all you have?
On October 15 he handed in his outline. It argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues 'epistemological paralysis' and never mentions cowardice.

Students change their minds between an outline and an essay, Hale; that's called thinking. I'll want the outline and that version history in an email, with dates. And whatever happens next, this stays off his record and it stays quiet.
The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. You can search the play yourself.
I'll search it myself tonight, and a misquoted line is a citation error until someone proves otherwise. Fine, Hale. What are you putting on the table?
I'm not calling Owen a liar. I'm telling you what the document shows.
Good, because nobody in this room is. Then stop describing documents and give me terms, Hale. Policy 4.4 exists; is that what you're offering, or not?
Here's his in-class writing from September 24 next to it.

September 24, in class, under a clock, against something written at home; I'm writing the date down. Tell me what you think I'm looking at, Hale, because a side-by-side isn't a document until someone says what it proves. And I'm still waiting on terms.
The school's policy for a first concern is a supervised rewrite. If the rewrite holds up, nothing goes on his record.

To put this behind him, I'll accept a supervised rewrite, private, not in front of his class, and its mark replaces the zero. I want "nothing goes on his record" in an email from you tonight, cc the principal. And it happens well before December 1, Hale, because his scholarship applications won't wait for this school a second time.
He would do it at lunch in my room, not in front of the class.
Okay. Which day, and who else is in the room besides you? Put both in that email.
What would you need from me to be comfortable with that?

I'm not looking to be comfortable, Hale; I'm looking for it in writing. The day, the lunch hour, your room, the mark replacing the zero, and nothing on his record, all in one email tonight with the principal copied. And until he writes it, that zero comes out of the gradebook, because he shouldn't have to look at it on his phone again. Ten minutes.
I can put that in an email to you tonight.
Okay. Tonight, then, with the principal copied and every one of those terms in it. Anything else, Hale?
Is there anything else you want me to include?
No. Send it tonight, exactly as agreed, and I'll read every word.
Then I'll send it by eight.
By eight tonight. I'm writing that down, Hale.
Thank you for coming in.
Okay. A supervised rewrite at lunch in your room, its mark replacing the zero, nothing on his record, all in writing by eight tonight.
I'll see Owen tomorrow at lunch.
Tomorrow at lunch. Then that goes in the email by eight too, Hale.
